context.problem_statement: Compare three imputation strategies on the provided clinical dataset which has approximately 25% missing values in the 'cholesterol' and 'glucose' columns. Apply (1) mean imputation, (2) median imputation, and (3) KNN imputation (k=5). For each strategy, report the imputed mean and standard deviation of the affected columns. Then evaluate which strategy minimizes the RMSE against a held-out complete subset (rows 1-5, which have no missing values — remove them before imputing, then compare imputed vs original).
context.expert_knowledge: Use sklearn.impute: SimpleImputer for mean/median, KNNImputer for KNN. KNN imputation uses feature similarity and often outperforms simple strategies for clinical data with correlated variables. RMSE = sqrt(mean((imputed - original)^2)). Lower RMSE indicates better imputation quality.
